correctness.rationale: Every maximal geodesic has three vertices because the graph has diameter two and each edge extends to an induced shortest path. Six explicit labelled arrays have correct disjoint L-triples and optimal floor(area/3) counts; the residue decompositions tile all m,n≥2 into compatible bricks. Width-three columns consume all 3m cells, while width-two and width-four remainder counts are floor(2m/3) and floor(4m/3); in every n residue these sum exactly to floor(mn/3), matching the universal vertex upper bound. The actual standalone verifier passed six exact brick dynamic programs, 3481 constructive cases through size 60 by 60, and 14 independent exact maximum checks on small boards. These computations are supplementary, not an infinite proof.

General minmax frameworks require problem-specific evaluation; their accessible statements do not directly yield the brick construction. Full-text incompleteness is a residual risk.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The new theorem implies the earlier numerical upper bound on the square subfamily; the reverse is false without a lower-bound construction. originality.rationale: The 2022 original article, read in its 13-page open preprint, gives only a universal three-vertex upper bound for square rook-graph geodesic packing and separately computes the transversal number; its Proposition 2.6 and following paragraph do not construct optimum packings. A rectangular, all-residue optimal six-brick construction is not a rewording of those statements. A 2001 theorem on ordinary three-vertex paths in claw-free graphs counts potentially nongeodesic paths and therefore does not logically imply the present result. Older general induced-star-packing frameworks are sufficiently related to create residual overlap risk, which is expressly recorded; accessible abstracts do not state or directly imply the special exact equality. The search evidence alone is not treated as proof of uniqueness.
residual_risks: A specialization of general induced-star matching/minmax theorems could give the same rook-graph formula without explicit rook terminology; protected older full articles not inspected.

value.rationale: The 2022 article introduced the geodesic-packing problem and used square rook graphs specifically for an asymptotic packing-versus-hitting ratio, proving only the natural three-vertices-per-path upper bound. Establishing that it is attained in every rectangular shape fills a motivated exact-invariant gap for an unrestricted two-parameter infinite family, not an arbitrary finite slice. Six explicit bricks handle divisibility obstructions and yield a constructive linear-output-time optimum. The theorem is restricted to two nontrivial clique factors and does not enumerate optima.
